pr.title: ci: seed the PR AOT sccache after merges to main
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds `.github/workflows/aot-cache-seed.yml`, which fills the PR AOT lanes' sccache S3 cache right after merges to `main`.

**Why.** Pull requests from forks get no AWS credentials, so their `AOT Build Import` lanes read the cache but never write it. Until now only two kinds of runs wrote it: scheduled PR Test runs on `main`, and pull requests from branches in this repository. After a merge that changes a widely included header, every fork PR paid a cold AOT build until one of those happened to run. Measured on the PR Test runs after #9031 (rapidsai sccache fork) landed:

| | x64 lanes | arm64 lanes |
|---|---|---|
| Warm cache (median) | 13–14 min | 16–19 min |
| Cold, after a broad header change (#4312 changed `include/flashinfer/utils.cuh`) | 103–113 min | 125–214 min |

- **Gaps between cache writes:** the 3×/day scheduled runs started 5–7.5 h after their cron times.
- **Example:** on 11-12, fork PRs saw 17.7% cache hits from 17:50Z until a same-repo PR started rebuilding the cache at about 18:50Z.
- **Cost:** in the 40 h after the rollout settled, 25 fork PR runs hit a cold cache. That was about 143 extra runner-hours, or 85 a day.
- **Rollout window:** right after #9031 merged, PRs were cold for about 11 h. That was the stale `-rapids` prefix waiting for the first scheduled run.

**What the seed does**
- **Trigger:** runs on pushes to `main` that can change an AOT compile input:
  - `include/`, `csrc/`, `3rdparty/`
  - C/C++/CUDA sources and Jinja templates anywhere
  - `flashinfer/jit/`, `flashinfer/aot.py`, `flashinfer/compilation_context.py`, and `flashinfer/**/*jit*.py`
  - `flashinfer-jit-cache/`, `ci/docker-tags.yml`, `ci/cuda-versions.json`, and the two AOT scripts

  It can also be started with `workflow_dispatch`. It only runs in `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer`.
- **Same lanes:** it builds the same lanes as the PR AOT matrix (x64/arm64 × each runtime CUDA version with a published image). It uses the same image, runner pool and script (`task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh`), so it writes the `cuda<ver>-<arch>-rapids` prefixes the PR lanes read.
- **Credentials:** it runs with the sccache credentials and fails if they are missing, rather than doing a read-only build that seeds nothing.
- **Concurrency:** a single `aot-cache-seed` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so one seed runs and only the newest waits.
  - This answers why #6968 removed the per-merge PR Test runs: 90% of them were cancelled, and their work was lost.
  - Here nothing is lost. sccache uploads each object as soon as it compiles, so PRs started while a seed is still running already benefit. On 11-12, fork PR hit rates went 18% → 51% → 100% while a cache-writing run was still compiling.
- **`fail-fast: false`:** lanes write different prefixes, so one failing lane doesn't stop the others.
- **No lint:** the seed sets the new `AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT=1` switch, which skips the provider spec lint. The merged code already passed it on its PR, and a lint failure would leave the cache cold until the next merge. PR lanes are unchanged.
- **No other tests or reporting:** a seed builds and imports the provider wheels and nothing else, and opens no issue on failure. The scheduled PR Test run already reports AOT build breakage on `main`.

**Expected cost:** roughly 40–65 CPU runner-hours a day. Most seeds are warm runs of 13–19 min per lane, plus a few cold ones after broad header changes. This is an estimate: in the last 7 days, merges touching `include/`, `csrc/` or `3rdparty/` came a median 60 min apart. On the savings side, cold fork PRs currently cost about 85 extra runner-hours a day, and a cold PR waits 1.5–3.5 h for AOT instead of 15–20 min. Both figures come from 2 days of data with one broad header change, so the seed's own runtimes should be checked after it lands.

**What it does not fix:** PRs that start during the 2–3.5 h after a broad header change are still partly cold. The seed shortens that stretch by starting as soon as the change merges, instead of waiting for the next writer.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- Follow-up to #9031 (rapidsai sccache fork for the PR AOT lane).
- Context: #6968 (scheduled runs replaced the per-merge PR Test runs on `main`).
- The spec-lint lock-timeout flake from the same investigation is already fixed by #9441.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. (Ran on the changed files; all pass.)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed. (`tests/cpu/infra/test_aot_cache_seed_workflow.py`)
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.). (20 passed; see Reviewer Notes for how.)
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive; justify below).

  Suggested CI test targets (optional; paths under `tests/`, whitespace-separated — a starting

## 🔬 Experimental Track

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #

## Reviewer Notes

- **The workflow itself can't run on this PR.** It triggers only on `push` to `main`. The first real seed is the first matching merge after this lands. To check it, look for `sccache mode: read-write` and the `sccache-stats-seed-*` artifacts. After a header change, later fork PRs' AOT hit rates should go up.
- **New tests:** they check the triggers, that seeds never cancel, which paths start a seed and which don't (through a GitHub path-filter translator), that the lanes match the PR matrix, the credentials, and the lint switch (run as a bash fragment).
- **How I ran them:** in an isolated copy with only pytest and PyYAML, because my local machine has no torch and `tests/conftest.py` imports it. The CI CPU lane runs them normally.
- **Existing test:** `test_aot_script_lints_specs_before_building_and_inspects_wheels_after` still holds, since the lint call is still before the build.
- **actionlint:** it reports only the custom runner labels (`cpu`, `on-demand`) and SC2046 in the `Cleanup` step copied from `pr-test.yml`. `pr-test.yml` gets the same warnings.
- **Path filter:** this is a judgment call. A false positive costs one warm run (13–19 min per lane). A missed path means fork PRs stay cold until the next scheduled run.

+# Seeds the PR AOT lanes' sccache S3 cache after merges to main.
+#
+# Pull requests from forks build the AOT lanes read-only: they get no AWS
+# credentials, so they cannot write the cache. Before this workflow, only the
+# scheduled PR Test runs on main (three a day, often hours late) and pull
+# requests from branches in this repository wrote it. After a merge that changes
+# a widely included header, every fork pull request paid a cold build (about
+# 1.75 h on x64, 2-3.5 h on arm64, instead of 13-19 min) until one of those
+# writers happened to run.
+#
+# This runs the same AOT build as the PR lane on main, with write access, right
+# after each merge that can change compile inputs. sccache uploads every object
+# as soon as it is compiled, so a seed that is still running already speeds up
+# the pull requests started after it. The concurrency group never cancels: one
+# seed runs, and only the newest pending one waits. A seed after a broad header
+# change can therefore delay the next one, but none of its work is thrown away,
+# unlike the per-merge PR Test runs #6968 removed (90% were cancelled).
+#
+# A seed builds and imports the provider wheels but tests nothing else, and a
+# failure opens no issue: the scheduled PR Test run on main reports build
+# breakage. It skips the provider spec lint, which the merged code already passed
+# on its pull request.
+name: AOT Cache Seed
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    # Anything that can change an AOT compile command, a compiled source or
+    # the build image. A false positive costs one warm run (13-19 min per lane).
+    paths:
+      - 'include/**'
+      - 'csrc/**'
+      - '3rdparty/**'
+      - '**/*.cu'
+      - '**/*.cuh'
+      - '**/*.h'
+      - '**/*.hpp'
+      - '**/*.cpp'
+      - '**/*.cc'
+      - '**/*.inc'
+      - '**/*.jinja'
+      - 'flashinfer/aot.py'
+      # Pins the TRT-LLM manifests and export headers that kernels compile against.
+      - 'flashinfer/artifacts.py'
+      - 'flashinfer/compilation_context.py'
+      - 'flashinfer/jit/**'
+      - 'flashinfer/**/*jit*.py'
+      - 'flashinfer-jit-cache/**'
+      - 'ci/docker-tags.yml'
+      - 'ci/cuda-versions.json'
+      - 'scripts/jit_cache_build_common.sh'
+      - 'scripts/task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh'
+      - '.github/workflows/aot-cache-seed.yml'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+concurrency:
+  group: aot-cache-seed
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  setup:
+    name: Setup
+    # Forks have no cache credentials; a seed there would only build read-only.
+    if: github.repository == 'flashinfer-ai/flashinfer'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
+      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Get Docker Tag
+        id: get-tag
+        run: |
+          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
+          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      # Same lanes as the PR AOT matrix in pr-test.yml, so the seed writes the
+      # key prefixes those lanes read.
+      - name: Build seed matrix
+        id: matrix
+        run: |
+          MATRIX=$(
+            for arch in x64 arm64; do
+              for cuda in $(jq -r '.runtime[].label' ci/cuda-versions.json); do
+                if ! grep -q "^flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${cuda}:" ci/docker-tags.yml; then
+                  echo "::notice title=AOT image not published::Skipping ${cuda}" >&2
+                  continue
+                fi
+                jq -nc --arg arch "$arch" --arg cuda "$cuda" \
+                  '{name: "AOT Cache Seed (\($arch), \($cuda))", arch: $arch, cuda: $cuda}'
+              done
+            done | jq -sc '{include: .}'
+          )
+          echo "matrix=${MATRIX}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "${MATRIX}" | jq .
+
+  seed:
+    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
+    needs: setup
+    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, "${{ matrix.arch }}", cpu, on-demand]
+    timeout-minutes: 360
+    strategy:
+      # Lanes seed independent key prefixes; one failing must not stop the rest.
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
+    env:
+      DOCKER_IMAGE: flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${{ matrix.cuda }}:${{ needs.setup.outputs.docker_tag }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Cleanup
+        run: |
+          docker stop $(docker ps -q) 2>/dev/null || true
+          docker rm $(docker ps -aq) 2>/dev/null || true
+          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/* || true
+          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/.[!.]* || true
+          rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer_jit || true
+          docker image prune -f || true
+          docker builder prune -f --filter "until=24h" || true
+
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          # Self-hosted runners keep the workspace between jobs, so the token
+          # must not be left behind in .git/config.
+          persist-credentials: false
+          submodules: recursive
+
+      - name: Seed AOT sccache
+        env:
+          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET }}
+          SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION }}
+          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
+          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
+          AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY: ${{ vars.AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY || '2' }}
+        run: |
+          if [ -z "${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}" ] || [ -z "${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" ]; then
+            echo "::error::sccache credentials are missing; a read-only build would seed nothing"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
+          bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" \
+            -e SCCACHE_BUCKET "${SCCACHE_BUCKET}" \
+            -e SCCACHE_REGION "${SCCACHE_REGION}" \
+            -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
+            -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
+            -e SCCACHE_STATS_DIR /workspace/sccache-stats \
+            -e AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY "${AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY}" \
+            -e AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT 1 \
+            --no-gpu ./scripts/task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh
+
+      - name: Display sccache stats
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          STATS_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats/sccache-stats.txt"
+          if [ -s "${STATS_FILE}" ]; then
+            cat "${STATS_FILE}"
+          else
+            echo "::warning::sccache stats were not produced"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Upload sccache stats
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: sccache-stats-seed-${{ matrix.cuda }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
+          path: sccache-stats/
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+          retention-days: 14

+"""Contract checks for .github/workflows/aot-cache-seed.yml.
+
+The seed only helps if it writes the key prefixes the PR AOT lanes read, so it
+must run the same build script on the same lanes, with write credentials, and
+must never cancel a running seed (cancelled seeds were the failure mode of the
+per-merge PR Test runs that #6968 removed).
+"""
+
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+AOT_SCRIPT = "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh"
+
+
+def _workflow(name: str) -> dict:
+    yaml = pytest.importorskip("yaml")
+    return yaml.safe_load(
+        (REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    )
+
+
+def _triggers(workflow: dict) -> dict:
+    # PyYAML parses the bare `on:` key as boolean True.
+    return workflow.get("on", workflow.get(True))
+
+
+def test_seed_runs_after_merges_to_main_and_never_cancels():
+    workflow = _workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml")
+    triggers = _triggers(workflow)
+
+    assert set(triggers) == {"push", "workflow_dispatch"}
+    assert triggers["push"]["branches"] == ["main"]
+    assert workflow["concurrency"] == {
+        "group": "aot-cache-seed",
+        "cancel-in-progress": False,
+    }
+
+
+def _github_path_regex(pattern: str) -> "re.Pattern[str]":
+    """GitHub path filter syntax: `**` crosses directories, `*` does not."""
+    out = ""
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(pattern):
+        if pattern.startswith("**/", i):
+            out += "(?:.*/)?"
+            i += 3
+        elif pattern.startswith("**", i):
+            out += ".*"
+            i += 2
+        elif pattern[i] == "*":
+            out += "[^/]*"
+            i += 1
+        else:
+            out += re.escape(pattern[i])
+            i += 1
+    return re.compile(out + r"\Z")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "path",
+    [
+        "include/flashinfer/utils.cuh",
+        "csrc/page.cu",
+        "3rdparty/cutlass",
+        "flashinfer/jit/fused_moe.py",
+        "flashinfer/aot.py",
+        "flashinfer/artifacts.py",
+        "flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/cake_bf16_megamoe/shim/cake_jit.py",
+        "ci/docker-tags.yml",
+        "ci/cuda-versions.json",
+        f"scripts/{AOT_SCRIPT}",
+        "scripts/jit_cache_build_common.sh",
+    ],
+)
+def test_seed_triggers_on_compile_inputs(path):
+    patterns = _triggers(_workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml"))["push"]["paths"]
+    assert any(_github_path_regex(p).match(path) for p in patterns), path
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["README.md", "docs/index.rst", "tests/test_x.py"])
+def test_seed_ignores_unrelated_changes(path):
+    patterns = _triggers(_workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml"))["push"]["paths"]
+    assert not any(_github_path_regex(p).match(path) for p in patterns), path
+
+
+def test_seed_matches_pr_aot_lanes():
+    seed_jobs = _workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml")["jobs"]
+    pr_test = (REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "pr-test.yml").read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+
+    # Same runner pool and lane set as the PR AOT matrix.
+    assert seed_jobs["seed"]["runs-on"] == [
+        "self-hosted",
+        "linux",
+        "${{ matrix.arch }}",
+        "cpu",
+        "on-demand",
+    ]
+    assert '["self-hosted", "linux", $arch, "cpu", "on-demand"]' in pr_test
+    matrix_step = next(
+        s for s in seed_jobs["setup"]["steps"] if s.get("id") == "matrix"
+    )
+    assert "for arch in x64 arm64" in matrix_step["run"]
+    assert ".runtime[].label" in matrix_step["run"]
+    assert "ci/docker-tags.yml" in matrix_step["run"]
+    # One lane failing must not cancel the others.
+    assert seed_jobs["seed"]["strategy"]["fail-fast"] is False
+
+
+def test_seed_builds_with_write_credentials_and_skips_lint():
+    steps = _workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml")["jobs"]["seed"]["steps"]
+    seed = next(s for s in steps if s.get("name") == "Seed AOT sccache")
+
+    assert (
+        seed["env"]["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] == "${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}"
+    )
+    assert (
+        seed["env"]["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"]
+        == "${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}"
+    )
+    assert f"./scripts/{AOT_SCRIPT}" in seed["run"]
+    assert "-e AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT 1" in seed["run"]
+    # A missing secret must fail loudly instead of seeding nothing.
+    assert "credentials are missing" in seed["run"]
+
+
+def test_seed_only_runs_in_the_upstream_repository():
+    setup = _workflow("aot-cache-seed.yml")["jobs"]["setup"]
+    assert setup["if"] == "github.repository == 'flashinfer-ai/flashinfer'"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="runs a bash fragment")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("skip, linted", [("", True), ("0", True), ("1", False)])
+def test_aot_script_lint_switch(skip, linted):
+    """AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT=1 skips the lint but still prefetches its headers."""
+    text = (REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / AOT_SCRIPT).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    start = text.index('if [ "${AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT:-0}" = "1" ]; then')
+    end = text.index("\nfi\n", start) + len("\nfi\n")
+    fragment = (
+        'run_provider_spec_lint() { echo "LINT $*"; }\n'
+        'python3() { echo "PYTHON $*"; }\n'
+        "SCRIPT_DIR=/scripts\n"
+        "PROVIDER_ARCHITECTURE_LIST=(8.0 9.0a)\n" + text[start:end]
+    )
+    env = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin"}
+    if skip:
+        env["AOT_SKIP_SPEC_LINT"] = skip
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["bash", "-c", fragment], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, check=True
+    )
+    assert ("LINT 3 8.0 9.0a" in result.stdout) is linted
+    # The lint prefetches on its own; the skip path must do it explicitly.
+    prefetched = "PYTHON /scripts/prefetch_jit_spec_headers.py" in result.stdout
+    assert prefetched is not linted

Walkthrough

The change adds a workflow that seeds the AOT cache after qualifying pushes to `main` or manual dispatches. # CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"

      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
        id: cuda-versions
        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check Skip Conditions
        id: check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 0
          fi

          # Use PR event SHAs for reliable diff (avoids issues with origin refs)
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          # TODO (yongwww): Add back ^\.github/ before merging to main
          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"

          SKIP=true
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then
              SKIP=false
              break
            fi
          done <<< "$CHANGED"

          echo "skip=$SKIP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          if [ "$SKIP" == "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Skipping build - only docs/config files changed"
          fi

      # skip_aot / skip_gpu dispatch inputs have to drop entries before the
      # matrix expands - a job-level `if` cannot see the matrix context, and
      # skipping inside the job would still claim a runner first.
      - name: Build Test Matrix
        id: matrix
        env:
          SKIP_AOT: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_aot }}
          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
          # Targets requested by the triggering `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment,
          # already validated in the step above. Empty for an unparameterised run.
          REQUESTED_TEST_PATH: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
          H100_ON_PRS: 'true'
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          RUN_H100=false

          # gets the request as-is (its bare run covers tests/); A10G and T4 get it
          # intersected with their shard lists, and a lane left with nothing is skipped.
          # A10G is intersected per shard: each shard whose files overlap the request
          # runs as its own job, so a targeted run keeps the bare run's balancing and
          # -k splits, and shards left with nothing are not scheduled.

                --scripts "scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part${shard}.sh" \
                --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
              echo "A10G shard ${shard} targeted scope: ${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-<none: shard not scheduled>}"
            done
            T4_SCOPE=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
              --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh \
              --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
            echo "T4 targeted scope:   ${T4_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"

            # The H100 lane ignores it, so drop it from the H100 scope here: a
            # request naming only tests/cpu then schedules no H100 job instead of
            # one that collects nothing.

                    kind: "aot",
                    runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", $arch, "cpu", "on-demand"],
                    cuda: $cuda,
                    script: "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh",
                    timeout: 360

                gpu_name: "CPU",

                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
